newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest electricity steady in thin demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest electricity steady in thin demand.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Midwestern U.S. again held steady Wednesday in thin demand from mild fall weather, brokers and marketers said.
Prices through much of the Mid-West have held fairly steady through October, with players having sewn up monthly contracts in anticipation of scheduled power generation outages, the sources said.

In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR) district, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Thursday delivery were seen trading mostly stable around $16.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), with offers pegged near $17.00.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was talked steady in the $12.50-14.00 area, the sources said.
November ECAR prices were steady near $17.50, while December held at $19.00 and January/February business was assessed steady near $21.00 per MWh.
Peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) were talked slightly higher at $15.00-16.00 from discussion at $14.50-15.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power for Thursday delivery was assessed steady near $17.00, while off-peak next day power was pegged in the $11.50-13.00 range.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in the entire region was pegged at $17.00-21.00 from Tuesday talk at $17.00-19.00 in the northern area and $23.00-24.00 in the south.
Off-peak prices in SPP held steady in the $12.50-14.00 area.
November SPP was discussed near $18.50, while December was talked steady at $22.10-22.40, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
